terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: with an accusative, often with ex
evidence: Plaut. Am. 1.1.49: dēlēgit virōs prīmōrēs prīncipēs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Rosc. Am. 3 fin.: quī ex senātū in hoc cōnsilium dēlēctī estis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Pick the best or the fittest out of a number: men for a task, a leader, a place for a camp (Lewis & Short). Not to be confused with dēligāre, “tie fast”.

sources: Lewis & Short: eligo · Lewis & Short: deligo
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 359.
